articleTitle: On the Andreadakis Problem for Subgroups of IAn
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_n$</tex> be the free group on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> generators. Consider the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IA_n$</tex> of automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_n$</tex> acting trivially on its abelianization. There are two canonical filtrations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IA_n$</tex>: the 1st one is its lower central series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _*$</tex>; the 2nd one is the Andreadakis filtration <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A_*$</tex>, defined from the action on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_n$</tex>. The Andreadakis problem consists in understanding the difference between these filtrations. Here, we show that they coincide when restricted to the subgroup of triangular automorphisms and to the pure braid group.

articleTitle: Universal Behavior of the Corners of Orbital Beta Processes
abstract: There is a unique unitarily-invariant ensemble of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\times N$</tex> Hermitian matrices with a fixed set of real eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_1> \dots > a_N$</tex>. The joint eigenvalue distribution of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(N-1)$</tex> top-left principal submatrices of a random matrix from this ensemble is called the orbital unitary process. There are analogous matrix ensembles of symmetric and quaternionic Hermitian matrices that lead to the orbital orthogonal and symplectic processes, respectively. By extrapolation, on the dimension of the base field, of the explicit density formulas, we define the orbital beta processes. We prove the universal behavior of the virtual eigenvalues of the smallest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> principal submatrices, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> is independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and the eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_1> \dots > a_N$</tex> grow linearly in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and in such a way that the rescaled empirical measures converge weakly. The limiting object is the Gaussian beta corners process. As a byproduct of our approach, we prove a theorem on the asymptotics of multivariate Bessel functions.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Approximation on Affine Subspaces
abstract: We solve the convergence case of the generalized Baker–Schmidt problem for simultaneous approximation on affine subspaces, under natural diophantine type conditions. In one of our theorems, we do not require monotonicity on the approximation function. In order to prove these results, we establish asymptotic formulae for the number of rational points close to an affine subspace. One key ingredient is a sharp upper bound on a certain sum of reciprocals of fractional parts associated with the matrix defining the affine subspace.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to “Desingularizing $\boldsymbol{b}^{\boldsymbol{m}}$-Symplectic Structures”
On Analytic Todd Classes of Singular Varieties
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,h)$</tex> be a compact and irreducible Hermitian complex space. This paper is devoted to various questions concerning the analytic K-homology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,h)$</tex>. In the 1st part, assuming either <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim (\operatorname{sing}(X))=0$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim (X)=2$</tex>, we show that the rolled-up operator of the minimal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\partial }$</tex> complex, denoted here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\eth }_{\textrm{rel}}$</tex>, induces a class in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_0 (X)\equiv KK_0(C(X),\mathbb{C})$</tex>. A similar result, assuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim (\operatorname{sing}(X))=0$</tex>, is proved also for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\eth }_{\textrm{abs}}$</tex>, the rolled-up operator of the maximal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\partial }$</tex> complex. We then show that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim (\operatorname{sing}(X))=0$</tex> we have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\overline{\eth }_{\textrm{rel}}]=\pi _*[\overline{\eth }_M]$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi :M\rightarrow X$</tex> an arbitrary resolution and with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\overline{\eth }_M]\in K_0 (M)$</tex> the analytic K-homology class induced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\partial }+\overline{\partial }^t$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. In the 2nd part of the paper we focus on complex projective varieties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V,h)$</tex> endowed with the Fubini–Study metric. First, assuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim (V)\leq 2$</tex>, we compare the Baum–Fulton–MacPherson K-homology class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> with the class defined analytically through the rolled-up operator of any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\partial }$</tex> complex. We show that there is no <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\partial }$</tex> complex on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\operatorname{reg}(V),h)$</tex> whose rolled-up operator induces a K-homology class that equals the Baum–Fulton–MacPherson class. Finally in the last part of the paper we prove that under suitable assumptions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> the push-forward of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\overline{\eth }_{\textrm{rel}}]$</tex> in the K-homology of the classifying space of the fundamental group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> is a birational invariant.

articleTitle: An Extension of Weyl's Equidistribution Theorem to Generalized Polynomials and Applications
abstract: Generalized polynomials are mappings obtained from the conventional polynomials by the use of the operations of addition and multiplication and taking the integer part. Extending the classical theorem of Weyl on equidistribution of polynomials, we show that a generalized polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q(n)$</tex> has the property that the sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(q(n) \lambda )_{n \in \mathbf{Z}}$</tex> is well-distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bmod \, 1$</tex> for all but countably many <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \in{\mathbf R}$</tex> if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lim\nolimits _{\substack{|n| \rightarrow \infty \\ n \notin J}} |q(n)| = \infty $</tex> for some (possibly empty) set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> having zero natural density in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Z}$</tex>. We also prove a version of this theorem along the primes (which may be viewed as an extension of classical results of Vinogradov and Rhin). Finally, we utilize these results to obtain new examples of sets of recurrence and van der Corput sets.

articleTitle: A Basis of Casimirs in 3D Magnetohydrodynamics
abstract: We prove that any regular Casimir in 3D magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) is a function of the magnetic helicity and cross-helicity. In other words, these two helicities are the only independent regular integral invariants of the coadjoint action of the MHD group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SDiff}(M)\ltimes \mathfrak X^*(M)$</tex>, which is the semidirect product of the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and the dual space of its Lie algebra.

articleTitle: Equilibrium States on Right LCM Semigroup $C^*$-Algebras
abstract: We determine the structure of equilibrium states for a natural dynamics on the boundary quotient diagram of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebras for a large class of right LCM semigroups. The approach is based on abstract properties of the semigroup and covers the previous case studies on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{N}} \rtimes {\mathbb{N}}^\times$</tex>, dilation matrices, self-similar actions, and Baumslag–Solitar monoids. At the same time, it provides new results for right LCM semigroups associated to algebraic dynamical systems.

articleTitle: A Sharp Rearrangement Principle in Fourier Space and Symmetry Results for PDEs with Arbitrary Order
abstract: We prove sharp inequalities for the symmetric-decreasing rearrangement in Fourier space of functions in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>. Our main result can be applied to a general class of (pseudo-)differential operators in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex> of arbitrary order with radial Fourier multipliers. For example, we can take any positive power of the Laplacian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-\Delta )^s$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s> 0$</tex> and, in particular, any polyharmonic operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-\Delta )^m$</tex> with integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m \geqslant 1$</tex>. As applications, we prove radial symmetry and real-valuedness (up to trivial symmetries) of optimizers for (1) Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequalities with derivatives of arbitrary order, (2) ground states for bi- and polyharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations (NLS), and (3) Adams–Moser–Trudinger type inequalities for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$</tex> in any dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geqslant 1$</tex>. As a technical key result, we solve a phase retrieval problem for the Fourier transform in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>. To achieve this, we classify the case of equality in the corresponding Hardy–Littlewood majorant problem for the Fourier transform in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>.

articleTitle: Extremal Domains and Pólya-type Inequalities for the Robin Laplacian on Rectangles and Unions of Rectangles
abstract: We investigate the question of whether the eigenvalues of the Laplacian with Robin boundary conditions can satisfy inequalities of the same type as those in Pólya's conjecture for the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians and, if so, what form these inequalities should take. Motivated in part by Pólya's original approach and in part by recent analogous works treating the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians, we consider rectangles and unions of rectangles and show that for these two families of domains, for any fixed positive value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> of the boundary parameter, Pólya-type inequalities do indeed hold, albeit with an exponent smaller than that of the corresponding Weyl asympotics for a fixed domain. We determine the optimal exponents in both cases, showing that they are different in the two situations. Our approach to proving these results includes a characterization of the corresponding extremal domains for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k^{\textrm{}}$</tex>th eigenvalue in regions of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k,\alpha )$</tex>-plane, which in turn supports recent conjectures on the nature of the extrema among all bounded domains.

articleTitle: Parameter Spaces for Algebraic Equivalence
abstract: A cycle is algebraically trivial if it can be exhibited as the difference of two fibers in a family of cycles parameterized by a smooth integral scheme. Over an algebraically closed field, it is a result of Weil that it suffices to consider families of cycles parameterized by curves, or by abelian varieties. In this article, we extend these results to arbitrary base fields. The strengthening of these results turns out to be a key step in our work elsewhere extending Murre's results on algebraic representatives for varieties over algebraically closed fields to arbitrary perfect fields.

articleTitle: Complexity of Strong Approximation on the Sphere
abstract: By assuming some widely believed arithmetic conjectures, we show that the task of accepting a number that is representable as a sum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 2$</tex> squares subjected to given congruence conditions is NP-complete. On the other hand, we develop and implement a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that represents a number as a sum of four squares with some restricted congruence conditions, by assuming a polynomial-time algorithm for factoring integers and Conjecture 1.1. As an application, we develop and implement a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for navigating Lubotzky, Phillips, Sarnak (LPS) Ramanujan graphs, under the same assumptions.

articleTitle: Pattern Equivariant Mass Transport in Aperiodic Tilings and Cohomology
abstract: Suppose that we have a repetitive and aperiodic tiling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{T}}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^n$</tex> and two mass distributions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_2$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^n$</tex>, each pattern equivariant (PE) with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{T}}$</tex>. Under what circumstances is it possible to do a bounded transport from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_1$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_2$</tex>? When is it possible to do this transport in a strongly or weakly PE way? We reduce these questions to properties of the Čech cohomology of the hull of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{T}}$</tex>, properties that in most common examples are already well understood.

articleTitle: Corrigendum: “Mutations of Splitting Maximal Modifying Modules: The Case of Reflexive Polygons”
Monotone Lagrangians in Flag Varieties
abstract: In this paper, we give a formula for the Maslov index of a gradient holomorphic disk, which is a relative version of the Chern number formula of a gradient holomorphic sphere for a Hamiltonian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-action. Using the formula, we classify all monotone Lagrangian fibers of Gelfand–Cetlin systems on partial flag manifolds.

articleTitle: P-Partitions and Quasisymmetric Power Sums
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P, \omega )$</tex>-partition generating function of a labeled poset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P, \omega )$</tex> is a quasisymmetric function enumerating certain order-preserving maps from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Z}}^+$</tex>. We study the expansion of this generating function in the recently introduced type 1 quasisymmetric power sum basis <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\psi _{\alpha }\}$</tex>. Using this expansion, we show that connected, naturally labeled posets have irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>-partition generating functions. We also show that series-parallel posets are uniquely determined by their partition generating functions. We conclude by giving a combinatorial interpretation for the coefficients of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi _{\alpha }$</tex>-expansion of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P, \omega )$</tex>-partition generating function akin to the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule.

articleTitle: Integral Hasse Principle and Strong Approximation for Markoff Surfaces
abstract: We study the failure of the integral Hasse principle and strong approximation for Markoff surfaces, as studied by Ghosh and Sarnak, using the Brauer–Manin obstruction.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Estimates for the Willmore Flow With Small Energy
abstract: Kuwert and Schätzle showed in 2001 that the Willmore flow converges to a standard round sphere, if the initial energy is small. In this situation, we prove stability estimates for the barycenter and the quadratic moment of the surface. Moreover, in codimension one, we obtain stability bounds for the enclosed volume and averaged mean curvature. As direct applications, we recover a quasi-rigidity estimate due to De Lellis and Müller (2006) and an estimate for the isoperimetric deficit by Röger and Schätzle (2012), whose original proofs used different methods.

articleTitle: Uniqueness of Polarization for the Autonomous 4-dimensional Painlevé-type Systems
abstract: We prove that for any autonomous 4-dimensional integral system of Painlevé type, the Jacobian of the generic spectral curve has a unique polarization, and thus by Torelli's theorem cannot be isomorphic as an unpolarized abelian surface to any other Jacobian. This enables us to identify the spectral curve and any irreducible genus 2 component of the boundary of an affine patch of the Liouville torus.

articleTitle: Buryak–Okounkov Formula for the n-Point Function and a New Proof of the Witten Conjecture
abstract: We identify the formulas of Buryak and Okounkov for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-point functions of the intersection numbers of psi-classes on the moduli spaces of curves. This allows us to combine the earlier known results and this one into a principally new proof of the famous Witten conjecture/Kontsevich theorem, where the link between the intersection theory of the moduli spaces and integrable systems is established via the geometry of double ramification cycles.

articleTitle: Removal Lemmas with Polynomial Bounds
abstract: A common theme in many extremal problems in graph theory is the relation between local and global properties of graphs. One of the most celebrated results of this type is the Ruzsa–Szemerédi triangle removal lemma, which states that if a graph is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon $</tex>-far from being triangle free, then most subsets of vertices of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(\varepsilon )$</tex> are not triangle free. Unfortunately, the best known upper bound on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(\varepsilon )$</tex> is given by a tower-type function, and it is known that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(\varepsilon )$</tex> is not polynomial in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon ^{-1}$</tex>. The triangle removal lemma has been extended to many other graph properties, and for some of them the corresponding function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(\varepsilon )$</tex> is polynomial. This raised the natural question, posed by Goldreich in 2005 and more recently by Alon and Fox, of characterizing the properties for which one can prove removal lemmas with polynomial bounds. Our main results in this paper are new sufficient and necessary criteria for guaranteeing that a graph property admits a removal lemma with a polynomial bound. Although both are simple combinatorial criteria, they imply almost all prior positive and negative results of this type. Moreover, our new sufficient conditions allow us to obtain polynomially bounded removal lemmas for many properties for which the previously known bounds were of tower type. In particular, we show that every semi-algebraic graph property admits a polynomially bounded removal lemma. This confirms a conjecture of Alon.

articleTitle: Generic Quantum Metric Rigidity
abstract: We introduce the coherent algebra of a compact metric measure space by analogy with the corresponding concept for a finite graph. As an application we show that upon topologizing the collection of isomorphism classes of compact metric measure spaces appropriately, the subset consisting of those with trivial compact quantum automorphism group is of 2nd Baire category. The latter result can be paraphrased as saying that “most” compact metric measure spaces have no (quantum) symmetries; in particular, they also have trivial ordinary (i.e., classical) automorphism group.

articleTitle: The Focusing Energy-Critical Nonlinear Wave Equation With Random Initial Data
abstract: We consider the focusing energy-critical quintic nonlinear wave equation in 3D Euclidean space. It is known that this equation admits a one-parameter family of radial stationary solutions, called solitons, which can be viewed as a curve in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \dot H^s_x({{\mathbb{R}}}^3) \times H^{s-1}_x({{\mathbb{R}}}^3)$</tex>, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s> 1/2$</tex>. By randomizing radial initial data in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \dot H^s_x({{\mathbb{R}}}^3) \times H^{s-1}_x({{\mathbb{R}}}^3)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s> 5/6$</tex>, which also satisfy a certain weighted Sobolev condition, we produce with high probability a family of radial perturbations of the soliton that give rise to global forward-in-time solutions of the focusing nonlinear wave equation that scatter after subtracting a dynamically modulated soliton. Our proof relies on a new randomization procedure using distorted Fourier projections associated to the linearized operator around a fixed soliton. To our knowledge, this is the 1st long-time random data existence result for a focusing wave or dispersive equation on Euclidean space outside the small data regime.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to “Sums of Kloosterman Sums over Arithmetic Progressions”
Resolutions With Conical Slices and Descent for the Brauer Group Classes of Certain Central Reductions of Differential Operators in Characteristic p
abstract: “Even more so is the word ‘crystalline’, a glacial and impersonal concept of his which disdains viewing existence from a single portion of time and space” Eileen Myles, “The Importance of Being Iceland” For a smooth variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> to a differential 1-form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> on the Frobenius twist <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{\textrm{(1)}}$</tex> one can associate an Azumaya algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{D}}}_{X,\alpha }$</tex>, defined as a certain central reduction of the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{D}}}_X$</tex> of “crystalline differential operators” on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. For a resolution of singularities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi :X\to Y$</tex> of an affine variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, we study for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> the class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{{\mathcal{D}}}_{X,\alpha }]$</tex> in the Brauer group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Br}(X^{\textrm{(1)}})$</tex> descends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y^{\textrm{(1)}}$</tex>. In the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is symplectic, this question is related to Fedosov quantizations in characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and the construction of noncommutative resolutions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. We prove that the classes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{{\mathcal{D}}}_{X,\alpha }]$</tex> descend étale locally for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{O}}}_Y\widetilde{\rightarrow }\pi _\ast{{\mathcal{O}}}_X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{1}\pi _*\mathcal O_X = R^2\pi _*\mathcal O_X =0$</tex>. We also define a certain class of resolutions, which we call resolutions with conical slices, and prove that for a general reduction of a resolution with conical slices in characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> to an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> classes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{{\mathcal{D}}}_{X,\alpha }]$</tex> descend to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y^{\textrm{(1)}}$</tex> globally for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>. Finally we give some examples; in particular, we show that Slodowy slices, Nakajima quiver varieties, and hypertoric varieties are resolutions with conical slices.

articleTitle: Hochschild Cohomology of Projective Hypersurfaces
abstract: We compute Hochschild cohomology of projective hypersurfaces starting from the Gerstenhaber–Schack complex of the (restricted) structure sheaf. We are particularly interested in the second cohomology group and its relation with deformations. We show that a projective hypersurface is smooth if and only if the classical HKR decomposition holds for this group. In general, the first Hodge component describing scheme deformations has an interesting inner structure corresponding to the various ways in which first order deformations can be realized: deforming local multiplications, deforming restriction maps, or deforming both. We make our computations precise in the case of quartic hypersurfaces, and compute explicit dimensions in many examples.

articleTitle: Hardy–Orlicz Spaces of Dirichlet Series: An Interpolation Problem on Abscissae of Convergence
abstract: The study of Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{H}^p$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\geq 1$</tex>) was initiated in [7] when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=\infty $</tex>, and in [2] for the general case. In this paper we introduce the Orlicz version of spaces of Dirichlet series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{H}^\psi $</tex>. We focus on the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi =\psi _q(t)=\exp (t^q)-1,$</tex> and we compute the abscissa of convergence for these spaces. It turns out that its value is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\min \{1/q\,,1/2\}$</tex> filling the gap between the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{H}^\infty $</tex>, where the abscissa is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>, and the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{H}^p$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> finite, where the abscissa is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/2$</tex>. The upper-bound estimate relies on an elementary method that applies to many spaces of Dirichlet series. This answers a question raised by Hedenmalm in [6].

articleTitle: Tame Tori in p-Adic Groups and Good Semisimple Elements
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be a reductive group over a non-archimedean local field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. We provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for all tori of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> to split over a tamely ramified extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. We then show the existence of good semisimple elements in every Moy–Prasad filtration coset of the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(k)$</tex> and its Lie algebra, assuming the above sufficient conditions are met.

articleTitle: On the Motivic Class of the Classifying Stack of $G_2$ and the Spin Groups
abstract: We compute the class of the classifying stack of the exceptional algebraic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_2$</tex> and of the spin groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Spin}_7$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Spin}_8$</tex> in the Grothendieck ring of stacks, and show that they are equal to the inverse of the class of the corresponding group. Furthermore, we show that the computation of the motivic classes of the stacks <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B}\mathrm{Spin}_n$</tex> can be reduced to the computation of the classes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B} \Delta_n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta_n\subset \mathrm{Pin}_n$</tex> is the “extraspecial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-group”, the preimage of the diagonal matrices under the projection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Pin}_n\to \mathrm{O}_n$</tex> to the orthogonal group.

articleTitle: Some Remarks on Non-Symmetric Interpolation Macdonald Polynomials
abstract: We provide elementary identities relating the three known types of non-symmetric interpolation Macdonald polynomials. In addition we derive a duality for non-symmetric interpolation Macdonald polynomials. We consider some applications of these results, in particular to binomial formulas involving non-symmetric interpolation Macdonald polynomials.

articleTitle: The Elliptic Tail Kernel
abstract: We introduce and study a new family of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-translation-invariant determinantal point processes on the two-sided <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-lattice. We prove that these processes are limits of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$zw$</tex> measures, which arise in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-deformation of harmonic analysis on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\infty )$</tex>, and express their correlation kernels in terms of Jacobi theta functions. As an application, we show that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$zw$</tex> measures are diffuse. Our results also hint at a link between the two-sided <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-lattice and rows/columns of Young diagrams.

articleTitle: The Brauer Group of the Universal Moduli Space of Vector Bundles Over Smooth Curves
abstract: We compute the Brauer group of the universal moduli stack of vector bundles on (possibly marked) smooth curves of genus at least three over the complex numbers. As consequence, we obtain an explicit description of the Brauer group of the smooth locus of the associated moduli space of semistable vector bundles, when the genus is at least four.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to: Finite Generation of the Algebra of Type A Conformal Blocks via Birational Geometry
Right Unimodal and Bimodal Singularities in Positive Characteristic
abstract: The problem of classification of real and complex singularities was initiated by Arnol’d in the sixties who classified simple, unimodal, and bimodal singularities w.r.t. right equivalence. The classification of simple singularities positive characteristic was achieved by Greuel and the author in 2014. In this article, we classify right unimodal and bimodal singularities in positive characteristic by giving explicit normal forms. It is surprising that in positive characteristic, there are no infinite series of unimodal and bimodal singularities. Moreover, the Milnor number of simple, unimodal, and bimodal singularity satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu(\,f)\leq 4p$</tex>. As an application we prove that, for singularities of right modality at most 2, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>-constant stratum is smooth and its dimension is equal to the right modality.

articleTitle: Existence of Cocompact Lattices in Lie Groups With a Bi-invariant Metric of Index 2
abstract: We study the existence of cocompact lattices in Lie groups with bi-invariant metric of signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,n-2)$</tex>. We assume in addition that the Lie groups under consideration are simply-connected, indecomposable, and solvable. Then their centre is one- or two-dimensional. In both cases, a parametrisation of the set of such Lie groups is known. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a lattice in terms of these parameters. For groups with one-dimensional centre this problem is related to Salem numbers.

articleTitle: Critical Exponent and Hausdorff Dimension in Pseudo-Riemannian Hyperbolic Geometry
abstract: The aim of this article is to understand the geometry of limit sets in pseudo-Riemannian hyperbolic geometry. We focus on a class of subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{PO}(p,q+1)$</tex> introduced by Danciger, Guéritaud, and Kassel, called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{H}}^{p,q}$</tex>-convex cocompact. We define a pseudo-Riemannian analogue of critical exponent and Hausdorff dimension of the limit set. We show that they are equal and bounded from above by the usual Hausdorff dimension of the limit set. We also prove a rigidity result in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{H}}^{2,1}={\mathbb{A}}\textrm{d}{\mathbb{S}}^3$</tex>, which can be understood as a Lorentzian version of a famous Theorem of R. Bowen in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>D hyperbolic geometry.

articleTitle: SIC-POVMs and the Stark Conjectures
abstract: The existence of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d^2$</tex> pairwise equiangular complex lines [equivalently, a symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM)] in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional Hilbert space is known only for finitely many dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>. We prove that, if there exists a set of real units in a certain ray class field (depending on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>) satisfying certain algebraic properties, a SIC-POVM exists, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is an odd prime congruent to 2 modulo 3. We give an explicit analytic formula that we expect to yield such a set of units. Our construction uses values of derivatives of zeta functions at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s=0$</tex> and is closely connected to the Stark conjectures over real quadratic fields. We verify numerically that our construction yields SIC-POVMs in dimensions 5, 11, 17, and 23, and we give the first exact SIC-POVM in dimension 23.

articleTitle: Reducibility of Schrödinger Equation on the Sphere
abstract: In this article we prove a reducibility result for the linear Schrödinger equation on the sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^n$</tex> with quasi-periodic in time perturbation. Our result includes the case of unbounded perturbation that we assume to be of order strictly less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/2$</tex> and satisfying some parity condition. As far as we know, this is one of the few reducibility results for an equation in more than one dimension with unbounded perturbations. Letus note that, surprisingly, our result does not require the use of the pseudo-differential calculus although the perturbation is unbounded.

articleTitle: The Mutual Singularity of Harmonic Measure and Hausdorff Measure of Codimension Smaller than One
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$</tex> be open and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E\subset \partial \Omega $</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0<{\mathcal{H}}^s(E)<\infty $</tex>, for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s\in (n,n+1)$</tex>, satisfy a local capacity density condition. In this paper it is shown that the harmonic measure cannot be mutually absolutely continuous with the Hausdorff measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{H}}^s$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>. This answers a question of Azzam and Mourgoglou, who had proved the same result under the additional assumption that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega $</tex> is a uniform domain.

articleTitle: Spectrality of Polytopes and Equidecomposability by Translations
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> be a polytope in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^d$</tex> (not necessarily convex or connected). We say that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is spectral if the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2(A)$</tex> has an orthogonal basis consisting of exponential functions. A result due to Kolountzakis and Papadimitrakis (2002) asserts that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is a spectral polytope, then the total area of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d-1)$</tex>-dimensional faces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> on which the outward normal is pointing at a given direction, must coincide with the total area of those <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d-1)$</tex>-dimensional faces on which the outward normal is pointing at the opposite direction. In this paper, we prove an extension of this result to faces of all dimensions between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d-1$</tex>. As a consequence we obtain that any spectral polytope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> can be dissected into a finite number of smaller polytopes, which can be rearranged using translations to form a cube.

articleTitle: Analytic Twists of GL3 × GL2 Automorphic Forms
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex> be a Hecke–Maass cusp form for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$</tex> with normalized Hecke eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{\pi }(n,r)$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> be a holomorphic or Maass cusp form for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$</tex> with normalized Hecke eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _f(n)$</tex>. In this paper, we are concerned with obtaining nontrivial estimates for the sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{align*}& \sum_{r,n\geq 1}\lambda_{\pi}(n,r)\lambda_f(n)e\left(t\,\varphi(r^2n/N)\right)V\left(r^2n/N\right), \end{align*}$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e(x)=e^{2\pi ix}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V(x)\in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty }(0,\infty )$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\geq 1$</tex> is a large parameter and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi (x)$</tex> is some real-valued smooth function. As applications, we give an improved subconvexity bound for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_3\times \textrm{GL}_2$</tex>  <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-aspect and under the Ramanujan--Petersson conjecture we derive the following bound for sums of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_3\times \textrm{GL}_2$</tex> Fourier coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{align*}& \sum_{r^2n\leq x}\lambda_{\pi}(r,n)\lambda_f(n)\ll_{\pi, f, \varepsilon} x^{5/7-1/364+\varepsilon} \end{align*}$$</tex>for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon>0$</tex>, which breaks for the 1st time the barrier <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(x^{5/7+\varepsilon })$</tex> in a work by Friedlander–Iwaniec.

articleTitle: Eremenko's Conjecture for Functions with Real Zeros: The Role of the Minimum Modulus
abstract: We consider the class of real transcendental entire functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> of finite order with only real zeros and show that if the iterated minimum modulus tends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex>, then the escaping set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I(\,f)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> has the structure of a spider's web, in which case Eremenko's conjecture holds. This minimum modulus condition is much weaker than that used in previous work on Eremenko's conjecture. For functions in this class, we analyse the possible behaviours of the iterated minimum modulus in relation to the order of the function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>.

articleTitle: Finite-Gap CMV Matrices: Periodic Coordinates and a Magic Formula
abstract: We prove a bijective unitary correspondence between (1) the isospectral torus of almost-periodic, absolutely continuous CMV matrices having fixed finite-gap spectrum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textsf{E}}$</tex> and (2) special periodic block-CMV matrices satisfying a Magic Formula. This latter class arises as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textsf{E}}$</tex>-dependent operator Möbius transforms of certain generating CMV matrices that are periodic up to a rotational phase; for this reason we call them “MCMV.” Such matrices are related to a choice of orthogonal rational functions on the unit circle, and their correspondence to the isospectral torus follows from a functional model in analog to that of GMP matrices. As a corollary of our construction we resolve a conjecture of Simon; namely, that Caratheodory functions associated to such CMV matrices arise as quadratic irrationalities.

articleTitle: Integrability of Dispersionless Hirota-Type Equations and the Symplectic Monge–Ampère Property
abstract: We prove that integrability of a dispersionless Hirota-type equation implies the symplectic Monge–Ampère property in any dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 4$</tex>. In 4D, this yields a complete classification of integrable dispersionless partial differential equations (PDEs) of Hirota type through a list of heavenly type equations arising in self-dual gravity. As a by-product of our approach, we derive an involutive system of relations characterizing symplectic Monge–Ampère equations in any dimension. Moreover, we demonstrate that in 4D the requirement of integrability is equivalent to self-duality of the conformal structure defined by the characteristic variety of the equation on every solution, which is in turn equivalent to the existence of a dispersionless Lax pair. We also give a criterion of linearizability of a Hirota-type equation via flatness of the corresponding conformal structure and study symmetry properties of integrable equations.

articleTitle: Prescribing Morse Scalar Curvatures: Blow-Up Analysis
abstract: We study finite-energy blow-ups for prescribed Morse scalar curvatures in both the subcritical and the critical regime. After general considerations on Palais–Smale sequences, we determine precise blow-up rates for subcritical solutions: in particular the possibility of tower bubbles is excluded in all dimensions. In subsequent papers, we aim to establish the sharpness of this result, proving a converse existence statement, together with a one-to-one correspondence of blowing-up subcritical solutions and critical points at infinity. This analysis will be then applied to deduce new existence results for the geometric problem.

articleTitle: On Subharmonic and Entire Functions of Small Order: After Kjellberg
abstract: We give a general method for constructing examples of transcendental entire functions of given small order, which allows precise control over the size and shape of the set where the minimum modulus of the function is relatively large. Our method involves a novel technique to obtain an upper bound for the growth of a positive harmonic function defined in a certain type of multiply connected domain, based on comparing the Harnack metric and hyperbolic metric, which gives a sharp estimate for the growth in many cases. Dedicated to the memory of Paddy Barry.

articleTitle: Vertex Algebras Associated with Hypertoric Varieties
abstract: We construct a family of vertex algebras associated with a family of symplectic singularity/resolution, called hypertoric varieties. While the hypertoric varieties are constructed by a certain Hamiltonian reduction associated with a torus action, our vertex algebras are constructed by (semi-infinite) BRST reduction. The construction works algebro-geometrically, and we construct sheaves of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbar $</tex>-adic vertex algebras over hypertoric varieties, which localize the vertex algebras. We determine when it is a vertex operator algebra by giving an explicit conformal vector. We also discuss the Zhu algebra of the vertex algebra and its relation with a quantization of the hypertoric variety. In certain cases, we obtain the affine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{W}}$</tex>-algebra associated with the subregular nilpotent orbit in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}_N$</tex> at level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N-1$</tex> and simple affine vertex operator algebra for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}_N$</tex> at level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Fourier Transform of Regularized Bessel Functions on Complex Numbers and Beyond Endoscopy Over Number Fields
abstract: In this article, we prove certain Weber–Schafheitlin-type integral formulae for Bessel functions over complex numbers. A special case is a formula for the Fourier transform of regularized Bessel functions on complex numbers. This is applied to extend the work of A. Venkatesh on Beyond Endoscopy for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Sym}^2$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_2$</tex> from totally real to arbitrary number fields.

articleTitle: Corrigendum and Addendum to “Polarized Parallel Transport and Uniruled Divisors on Generalized Kummer Varieties”
abstract: We correct the statement of the main result of [9] and provide some further precisions.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to “The Geometric Structure of Symplectic Contraction”
2-torsion points on theta divisors
abstract: In this note we prove a sharp bound for the number of 2-torsion points on a theta divisor and show that this is achieved only in the case of products of elliptic curves. This settles in the affirmative a conjecture of Marcucci and Pirola.

articleTitle: Periods and Reciprocity I
abstract: Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{F}$</tex> a number field with ring of integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{O}}_{\boldsymbol{F}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{p}},{\mathfrak{q}}$</tex> two coprime and squarefree ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{O}}_{\boldsymbol{F}}$</tex>, we prove a reciprocity relation for the 1st moment of the triple product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(\pi \otimes \pi _1\otimes \pi _2,\frac{1}{2})$</tex> twisted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{\pi }({\mathfrak{p}})$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _2$</tex> are fixed unitary automorphic representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{PGL}_2({\mathbb{A}}_{\boldsymbol{F}})$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _1$</tex> cuspidal and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> runs through unitary automorphic representations of conductor dividing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{q}}$</tex>. The method uses adelic integral representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions and the symmetric identity is established for a particular period. Finally, the integral period is connected to the moment via Parseval formula.

articleTitle: Equivalence of Sobolev Norms Involving Generalized Hardy Operators
abstract: We consider the fractional Schrödinger operator with Hardy potential and critical or subcritical coupling constant. This operator generates a natural scale of homogeneous Sobolev spaces, which we compare with the ordinary homogeneous Sobolev spaces. As a byproduct, we obtain generalized and reversed Hardy inequalities for this operator. Our results extend those obtained recently for ordinary (non-fractional) Schrödinger operators and have an important application in the treatment of large relativistic atoms.

articleTitle: A Note on the Dimension of the Largest Simple Hecke Submodule
abstract: For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\geq 2$</tex> even, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{k,N}$</tex> denote the dimension of the largest simple Hecke submodule of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{k}(\Gamma _0(N); {\mathbb{Q}})^{\textrm{new}}$</tex>. We show, using a simple analytic method, that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{k,N} \gg _k \log \log N / \log (2p)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, the smallest prime co-prime to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>. Previously, bounds of this quality were only known for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> in certain subsets of the primes. We also establish similar (and sometimes stronger) results concerning <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{k}(\Gamma _0(N), \chi )$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 2$</tex> an integer and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi $</tex> an arbitrary nebentypus.

articleTitle: The Brauer–Manin Obstruction for Zero-Cycles on K3 Surfaces
abstract: We study local–global principles for zero-cycles on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces defined over number fields. We follow an idea of Liang to use the trivial fibration over the projective line.

articleTitle: Tilting Bundles on Hypertoric Varieties
abstract: Recently McBreen and Webster constructed a tilting bundle on a smooth hypertoric variety (using reduction to finite characteristic) and showed that its endomorphism ring is Koszul. In this short note we present alternative proofs for these results. We simply observe that the tilting bundle constructed by Halpern-Leistner and Sam on a generic open Geometric Invariant Theory substack of the ambient linear space restricts to a tilting bundle on the hypertoric variety. The fact that the hypertoric variety is defined by a quadratic regular sequence then also yields an easy proof of Koszulity.

articleTitle: The Bounded Cohomology of SL$_{\textbf{2}}$ Over Local Fields and $\boldsymbol{S}$-Integers
abstract: It is proved that the continuous bounded cohomology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{SL}_2(k)$</tex> vanishes in all positive degrees whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is a non-Archimedean local field. This holds more generally for boundary-transitive groups of tree automorphisms and implies low degree vanishing for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{SL}_2$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>-integers.

articleTitle: Regulators of Elliptic Curves
abstract: We study the regulator of the Mordell–Weil group of elliptic curves over number fields, functions fields of characteristic 0 or function fields of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p>0$</tex>. We prove a new Northcott property for the regulator of elliptic curves of rank at least 4 defined over a number field. In the function field case, we obtain that non-trivial families of elliptic curves with bounded regulators and bounded ranks are limited families. We conclude by asking new questions.

articleTitle: Regularity and Multisecant Lines of Finite Schemes
abstract: For a nondegenerate finite subscheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb P}^c$</tex>, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm reg}(\Gamma)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell (\Gamma)$</tex> be, respectively, the regularity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> and the largest integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> such that there exists an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex>-secant line to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex>. It is always true that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm reg}(\Gamma) \geq \ell (\Gamma)$</tex>. In this article, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm reg}(\Gamma) \geq \frac{d-c+5}{2}$</tex> then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm reg}(\Gamma)$</tex> is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell (\Gamma)$</tex>. In addition, we describe the minimal free resolution of the homogeneous ideal of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> for the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm reg}(\Gamma) \geq \frac{d-c+5}{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Regularity Bootstrapping for 4th-order Nonlinear Elliptic Equations
abstract: We consider nonlinear 4th-order elliptic equations of double divergence type. We show that for a certain class of equations where the nonlinearity is in the Hessian, solutions that are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{2,\alpha }$</tex> enjoy interior estimates on all derivatives.

articleTitle: Dwork Crystals II
abstract: We give a generalization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic congruences for truncated period functions that were originally discovered for a class of hypergeometric functions by Bernard Dwork.

articleTitle: A Note on 1-Motives
abstract: We prove that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-motives defined over an algebraically closed subfield of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}$</tex>, viewed as Nori motives, the motivic Galois group coincides with the Mumford–Tate group. In particular, the Hodge realization of the Tannakian category of Nori motives generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-motives is fully faithful. This result extends an earlier result by the author, according to which Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are motivated (a weak form of the Hodge conjecture).

articleTitle: Desingularizing $\boldsymbol{b^m}$-Symplectic Structures
abstract: A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n$</tex>-dimensional Poisson manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M ,\Pi)$</tex> is said to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b^m$</tex>-symplectic if it is symplectic on the complement of a hypersurface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> and has a simple Darboux canonical form at points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> which we will describe below. In this article, we will discuss a desingularization procedure which, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> even, converts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi$</tex> into a family of symplectic forms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\epsilon}$</tex> having the property that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\epsilon}$</tex> is equal to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b^m$</tex>-symplectic form dual to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi$</tex> outside an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>-neighborhood of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> and, in addition, converges to this form as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> tends to zero in a sense that will be made precise in the theorem below. We will then use this construction to show that a number of somewhat mysterious properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b^m$</tex>-manifolds can be more clearly understood by viewing them as limits of analogous properties of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\epsilon}$</tex>'s. We will also prove versions of these results for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> odd; however, in the odd case the family <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\epsilon}$</tex> has to be replaced by a family of “folded” symplectic forms.

articleTitle: Star Bodies with Completely Symmetric Sections
abstract: We say that a star body <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is completely symmetric if it has centroid at the origin and its symmetry group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> forces any ellipsoid whose symmetry group contains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, to be a ball. In this short note, we prove that if all central sections of a star body <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> are completely symmetric, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> has to be a ball. A special case of our result states that if all sections of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> are origin symmetric and 1-symmetric, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> has to be a Euclidean ball. This answers a question from [12]. Our result is a consequence of a general theorem that we establish, stating that if the restrictions to almost all equators of a real function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> defined on the sphere, are isotropic functions, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is constant a.e. In the last section of this note, applications, improvements, and related open problems are discussed, and two additional open questions from [11] and [12] are answered.

articleTitle: Galois Conjugates of Pseudo-Anosov Stretch Factors are Dense in the Complex Plane
abstract: In this article, we study the Galois conjugates of stretch factors of pseudo-Anosov elements of the mapping class group of a surface. We show that—except in low-complexity cases—these conjugates are dense in the complex plane. For this, we use Penner's construction of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes. As a consequence, we obtain that in a sense there is no restriction on the location of Galois conjugates of stretch factors arising from Penner's construction. This complements an earlier result of Shin and the author stating that Galois conjugates of stretch factors arising from Penner's construction may never lie on the unit circle.

articleTitle: Splittings and Symbolic Powers of Square-free Monomial Ideals
abstract: We study the symbolic powers of square-free monomial ideals via symbolic Rees algebras and methods in prime characteristic. In particular, we prove that the symbolic Rees algebra and the symbolic associated graded algebra are split with respect to a morphism that resembles the Frobenius map and that exists in all characteristics. Using these methods, we recover a result by Hoa and Trung that states that the normalized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>-invariants and the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of the symbolic powers converge. In addition, we give a sufficient condition for the equality of the ordinary and symbolic powers of this family of ideals and relate it to Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture. Finally, we interpret this condition in the context of linear optimization.

articleTitle: Cantor Julia sets with Hausdorff dimension two
abstract: We prove the existence of Cantor Julia sets with Hausdorff dimension two. In particular, such examples can be found in cubic polynomials. The proof is based on the characterization of the parameter spaces and dynamical planes of cubic polynomials by Branner–Hubbard and the parabolic bifurcation theory developed by Shishikura in the 1990s.

articleTitle: Dimension Variation of Gouvêa–Mazur Type for Drinfeld Cuspforms of Level Γl(t)
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be a rational prime and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q>1$</tex> a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-power. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_k(\Gamma _1(t))$</tex> be the space of Drinfeld cuspforms of level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _1(t)$</tex> and weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}_q[t]$</tex>. For any non-negative rational number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, we denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d(k,\alpha )$</tex> the dimension of the slope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> generalized eigenspace for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex>-operator acting on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_k(\Gamma _1(t))$</tex>. In this paper, we prove a function field analogue of the Gouvêa–Mazur conjecture for this setting. Namely, we show that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \leqslant m$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_1,k_2>\alpha +1$</tex>, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_1\equiv k_2 \bmod p^m$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d(k_1,\alpha )=d(k_2,\alpha )$</tex>.

articleTitle: Einstein Four-Manifolds With Self-Dual Weyl Curvature of Nonnegative Determinant
abstract: We prove that simply connected Einstein four-manifolds of positive scalar curvature are conformally Kähler if and only if the determinant of the self-dual Weyl curvature is positive.

articleTitle: Smooth Travelling-Wave Solutions to the Inviscid Surface Quasi-Geostrophic Equation
abstract: We construct families of smooth travelling-wave solutions to the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic equation (SQG). These solutions can be viewed as the equivalents for this equation of the vortex anti-vortex pairs in the context of the incompressible Euler equation. Our argument relies on the stream function formulation and eventually amounts to solving a fractional nonlinear elliptic equation by variational methods.

articleTitle: On the Nonlinear Wave Equation with Time-periodic Potential
