abstract: It is known that for some time-periodic potentials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q(t, x) \geq 0$</tex> having compact support with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> some solutions of the Cauchy problem for the wave equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial _t^2 u - \Delta _x u + q(t,x)u = 0$</tex> have exponentially increasing energy as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \to \infty $</tex>. We show that if one adds a nonlinear defocusing interaction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|u|^ru, 2\leq r < 4,$</tex> then the solution of the nonlinear wave equation exists for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \in{\mathbb R}$</tex>, and its energy is polynomially bounded as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \to \infty $</tex> for every choice of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>. Moreover, we prove that the zero solution of the nonlinear wave equation is instable if the corresponding linear equation has the property mentioned above.

articleTitle: Quantum Variance for Eisenstein Series
abstract: In this paper, we prove an asymptotic formula for the quantum variance for Eisenstein series on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathbb{H}$</tex>. The resulting quadratic form is compared with the classical variance and the quantum variance for cusp forms. They coincide after inserting certain subtle arithmetic factors, including the central values of certain L-functions.

articleTitle: Minimal Newton Strata in Iwahori Double Cosets
abstract: The set of Newton strata in a given Iwahori double coset in the loop group of a reductive group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is indexed by a finite subset of the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(G)$</tex> of Frobenius-conjugacy classes. For unramified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, we show that it has a unique minimal element and determine this element. Under a regularity assumption, we also compute the dimension of the corresponding Newton stratum. We derive corresponding results for affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties.

articleTitle: The Orlicz Aleksandrov Problem for Orlicz Integral Curvature
abstract: In this paper, the Orlicz integral curvature is introduced, and some of its basic properties are discussed. The Orlicz Aleksandrov problem characterizing the Orlicz integral curvature is posed. The problem is solved in two situations when the given measure is even.

articleTitle: Singularities of Complex-Valued Solutions to Linear Parabolic Equations
abstract: We construct examples of complex-valued singular solutions to linear, uniformly parabolic equations with complex coefficients in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geq 2$</tex>, which are exactly as irregular as parabolic energy estimates allow.

articleTitle: Bubbling Phenomenon for Hermitian Yang–Mills Connections
abstract: We construct local examples of singular Hermitian Yang–Mills connections over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_1\subset \mathbb{C}^3$</tex> with uniformly bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-energy, but the number of essential singular points can be arbitrarily large.

articleTitle: Symbolic Powers of Ideals Defining F-pure and Strongly F-regular Rings
abstract: Given a radical ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex> in a regular ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>, the Containment Problem of symbolic and ordinary powers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex> consists of determining when the containment <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I^{(a)} \subseteq I^b$</tex> holds. By work of Ein–Lazersfeld–Smith, Hochster–Huneke and Ma–Schwede, there is a uniform answer to this question, but the resulting containments are not necessarily best possible. We show that a conjecture of Harbourne holds when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/I$</tex> is F-pure, and prove tighter containments in the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/I$</tex> is strongly F-regular.

articleTitle: Fundamental Inequality for Hyperbolic Coxeter and Fuchsian Groups Equipped with Geometric Distances
abstract: We prove that the hitting measure is not equivalent to the Lebesgue measure for a large class of nearest-neighbour random walks on hyperbolic reflection groups and Fuchsian groups with regular Dirichlet polygons.

articleTitle: A Riemann–Hilbert Problem Approach to Infinite Gap Hill's Operators and the Korteweg–de Vries Equation
abstract: We formulate the inverse spectral theory of infinite gap Hill's operators with bounded periodic potentials as a Riemann–Hilbert problem on a typically infinite collection of spectral bands and gaps. We establish a uniqueness theorem for this Riemann–Hilbert problem, which provides a new route to establishing unique determination of periodic potentials from spectral data. As the potentials evolve according to the Korteweg–de Vries Equation (KdV) equation, we use integrability to derive an associated Riemann–Hilbert problem with explicit time dependence. Basic principles from the theory of Riemann–Hilbert problems yield a new characterization of spectra for periodic potentials in terms of the existence of a solution to a scalar Riemann–Hilbert problem, and we derive a similar condition on the spectrum for the temporal periodicity for an evolution under the KdV equation.

articleTitle: Regularity Properties of Free Multiplicative Convolution on the Positive Line
abstract:
Given two nondegenerate Borel probability measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}_{+}=[0,\infty )$</tex>, we prove that their free multiplicative convolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu  oxtimes 
u$</tex> has zero singular continuous part and its absolutely continuous part has a density bounded by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x^{-1}$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u$</tex> are compactly supported Jacobi measures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0,\infty )$</tex> having power law behavior with exponents in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-1,1)$</tex>, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu  oxtimes 
u$</tex> is another Jacobi measure whose density has square root decay at the edges of its support.

articleTitle: The Anomaly Flow over Riemann Surfaces
abstract: We initiate the study of a new nonlinear parabolic equation on a Riemann surface. The evolution equation arises as a reduction of the Anomaly flow on a fibration. We obtain a criterion for long-time existence for this flow, and give a range of initial data where a singularity forms in finite time, as well as a range of initial data where the solution exists for all time. A geometric interpretation of these results is given in terms of the Anomaly flow on a Calabi–Yau three-fold.

articleTitle: On Helmholtz Equations and Counterexamples to Strichartz Estimates in Hyperbolic Space
abstract: In this paper, we study nonlinear Helmholtz equations<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \begin{equation} \tag{(NLH)} -\Delta_{\mathbb{H}^N} u - \frac{(N-1)^2}{4} u -\lambda^2 u = \Gamma|u|^{p-2}u \quad\text{in}\ \mathbb{H}^N, \;N\geq 2, \end{equation}$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta _{\mathbb {H}^N}$</tex> denotes the Laplace–Beltrami operator in the hyperbolic space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {H}^N$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \in L^\infty (\mathbb {H}^N)$</tex> is chosen suitably. Using fixed point and variational techniques, we find nontrivial solutions to (NLH) for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda>0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p>2$</tex>. The oscillatory behaviour and decay rate of radial solutions is analyzed, with extensions to Cartan–Hadamard manifolds and Damek–Ricci spaces. Our results rely on a new limiting absorption principle for the Helmholtz operator in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {H}^N$</tex>. As a byproduct, we obtain simple counterexamples to certain Strichartz estimates.

articleTitle: Linear Groups, Conjugacy Growth, and Classifying Spaces for Families of Subgroups
abstract: Given a group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> and a family of subgroups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}$</tex>, we consider its classifying space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathcal F}G$</tex> with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F = \mathcal{VC}yc$</tex> is the family of virtually cyclic subgroups, Juan-Pineda and Leary conjectured that a group admits a finite model for this classifying space if and only if it is virtually cyclic. By establishing a connection to conjugacy growth we can show that this conjecture holds for linear groups. We investigate a similar question that was asked by Lück–Reich–Rognes–Varisco for the family of cyclic subgroups. Finally, we construct finitely generated groups that exhibit wild inner automorphims but which admit a model for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathcal{VC}yc}(G)$</tex> whose 0-skeleton is finite.

articleTitle: Metrics of Constant Positive Curvature with Conical Singularities, Hurwitz Spaces, and Determinants of Laplacians
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: X\to {\Bbb C}P^1$</tex> be a meromorphic function of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> with simple poles and simple critical points on a compact Riemann surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf m$</tex> be the standard round metric of curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> on the Riemann sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Bbb C}P^1$</tex>. Then the pullback <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f^*\mathsf m$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf m$</tex> under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is a metric of curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> with conical singularities of conical angles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\pi$</tex> at the critical points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>. We study the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta$</tex>-regularized determinant of the Laplace operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> corresponding to the metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f^*\mathsf m$</tex> as a functional on the moduli space of the pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X, f)$</tex> (i.e., on the Hurwitz space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{g, N}(1, \dots, 1)$</tex>) and derive an explicit formula for the functional.

articleTitle: Duality for Commutative Group Stacks
abstract: We study in this article the dual of a (strictly) commutative group stack <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> and give some applications. Using the Picard functor and the Picard stack of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, we first give some sufficient conditions for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> to be dualizable. Then, for an algebraic stack <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> with suitable assumptions, we define an Albanese morphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_X: X\longrightarrow A^1(X)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^1(X)$</tex> is a torsor under the dual commutative group stack <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^0(X)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Pic}_{X/S}$</tex>. We prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_X$</tex> satisfies a natural universal property. We give two applications of our Albanese morphism. On the one hand, we give a geometric description of the elementary obstruction and of universal torsors (standard tools in the study of rational varieties over number fields). On the other hand, we give some examples of algebraic stacks that satisfy Grothendieck's section conjecture.

articleTitle: Quantum Q-Systems and Fermionic Sums—The Non-Simply Laced Case
abstract: In this paper, we seek to prove the equality of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-graded fermionic sums conjectured by Hatayama et al. [14] in its full generality, by extending the results of Di Francesco and Kedem [9] to the non-simply laced case. To this end, we will derive explicit expressions for the quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-system relations, which are quantum cluster mutations that correspond to the classical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-system relations, and write the identity of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-graded fermionic sums as a constant term identity. As an application, we will show that these quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-system relations are consistent with the short exact sequence of the Feigin–Loktev fusion product of Kirillov–Reshetikhin modules obtained by Chari and Venkatesh [5].

articleTitle: Finite Generation of the Algebra of Type A Conformal Blocks via Birational Geometry
abstract: We study the birational geometry of the moduli space of parabolic bundles over a projective line, in the framework of Mori's program. We show that the moduli space is a Mori dream space. As a consequence, we obtain the finite generation of the algebra of type A conformal blocks. Furthermore, we compute the H-representation of the effective cone that was previously obtained by Belkale. For each big divisor, the associated birational model is described in terms of moduli space of parabolic bundles.

articleTitle: Level Spacings and Nodal Sets at Infinity for Radial Perturbations of the Harmonic Oscillator
abstract: We study properties of the nodal sets of high-frequency eigenfunctions and quasimodes for radial perturbations of the harmonic oscillator. In particular, we consider nodal sets on spheres of large radius (in the classically forbidden region) for quasimodes with energies lying in intervals around a fixed energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>. For well-chosen intervals we show that these nodal sets exhibit quantitatively different behavior compared to those of the unperturbed harmonic oscillator. These energy intervals are defined via a careful analysis of the eigenvalue spacings for the perturbed operator, based on analytic perturbation theory and linearization formulas for Laguerre polynomials.

articleTitle: Computations of Eigenvalues and Resonances on Perturbed Hyperbolic Surfaces with Cusps
abstract: In this paper we describe a simple method that allows for a fast direct computation of the scattering matrix for a surface with hyperbolic cusps from the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map on the compact manifold with boundary obtained by removing the cusps. We illustrate that even if the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is obtained by a finite element method (FEM) one can achieve good accuracy for the scattering matrix. We give various interesting examples of how this can be used to investigate the behaviour of resonances under conformal perturbations or when moving in Teichmüller space. For example, based on numerical experiments we rediscover the four arithmetic surfaces of genus one with one cusp. This demonstrates that it is possible to identify arithmetic objects using FEM. All the videos accompanying this paper are available with its online version, or externally either at http://michaellevitin.net/hyperbolic.html or as a dedicated YouTube playlist.

articleTitle: Split Injectivity of A-Theoretic Assembly Maps
abstract: We construct an equivariant coarse homology theory arising from the algebraic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory of spherical group rings and use this theory to derive split injectivity results for associated assembly maps. On the way, we prove that the fundamental structural theorems for Waldhausen's algebraic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory functor carry over to its nonconnective counterpart defined by Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada.

articleTitle: Statistical Regularity of Apollonian Gaskets
abstract: Apollonian gaskets are formed by repeatedly filling the gaps between three mutually tangent circles with further tangent circles. In this paper we give explicit formulas for the limiting pair correlation and the limiting nearest neighbor spacing of centers of circles from a fixed Apollonian gasket. These are corollaries of the convergence of moments that we prove. The input from ergodic theory is an extension of Mohammadi–Oh's theorem on the equidisribution of expanding horospheres in the frame fundles of infinite volume hyperbolic spaces.

articleTitle: Derived Picard Groups of Preprojective Algebras of Dynkin Type
abstract: In this paper, we study two-sided tilting complexes of preprojective algebras of Dynkin type. We construct the most fundamental class of two-sided tilting complexes, which has a group structure by derived tensor products and induces a group of auto-equivalences of the derived category. We show that the group structure of the two-sided tilting complexes is isomorphic to the braid group of the corresponding folded graph. Moreover, we show that these two-sided tilting complexes induce tilting mutation and any tilting complex is given as the derived tensor products of them. Using these results, we determine the derived Picard group of preprojective algebras for type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Batalin–Vilkovisky Structure on the Tate–Hochschild Cohomology Ring of a Group Algebra
abstract: We determine the Batalin–Vilkovisky structure on the Tate–Hochschild cohomology of the group algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kG$</tex> of a finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> in terms of the additive decomposition. In particular, we show that the Tate cohomology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a Batalin–Vilkovisky subalgebra of the Tate–Hochschild cohomology of the group algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kG$</tex> and that the Tate cochain complex of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A_{\infty}}$</tex>-subalgebra of the Tate–Hochschild cochain complex of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kG$</tex>.

articleTitle: Hasse Principle for Rost Motives
abstract: We prove a Hasse principle for binary direct summands of the Chow motive of a smooth projective quadric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> over a number field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. Besides, we show that such summands are twists of Rost motives. In the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> has at most one real embedding we describe a complete motivic decomposition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>.

articleTitle: Uniform Bound for the Number of Rational Points on a Pencil of Curves
abstract: Consider a one-parameter family of smooth, irreducible, projective curves of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\ge 2$</tex> defined over a number field. Each fiber contains at most finitely many rational points by the Mordell conjecture, a theorem of Faltings. We show that the number of rational points is bounded only in terms of the family and the Mordell–Weil rank of the fiber's Jacobian. Our proof uses Vojta's approach to the Mordell Conjecture furnished with a height inequality due to the 2nd- and 3rd-named authors. In addition we obtain uniform bounds for the number of torsion points in the Jacobian that lie in each fiber of the family.

articleTitle: Ideal Simplicial Volume of Manifolds with Boundary
abstract: We define the ideal simplicial volume for compact manifolds with boundary. Roughly speaking, the ideal simplicial volume of a manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> measures the minimal size of possibly ideal triangulations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> “with real coefficients”, thus providing a variation of the ordinary simplicial volume defined by Gromov in 1982, the main difference being that ideal simplices are now allowed to appear in representatives of the fundamental class. We show that the ideal simplicial volume is bounded above by the ordinary simplicial volume, and that it vanishes if and only if the ordinary simplicial volume does. We show that, for manifolds with amenable boundary, the ideal simplicial volume coincides with the classical one, whereas for hyperbolic manifolds with geodesic boundary it can be strictly smaller. We compute the ideal simplicial volume of an infinite family of hyperbolic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifolds with geodesic boundary, for which the exact value of the classical simplicial volume is not known, and we exhibit examples where the ideal simplicial volume provides sharper bounds on mapping degrees than the classical simplicial volume.

articleTitle: Rational Links and DT Invariants of Quivers
abstract: We prove that the generating functions for the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of rational links are specializations of the generating functions of the motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants of appropriate quivers that we naturally associate with these links. This shows that the conjectural links–quivers correspondence of Kucharski–Reineke–Stošić–Sułkowski as well as the LMOV conjecture holds for all rational links. Along the way, we extend the links–quivers correspondence to tangles and, thus, explore elements of a skein theory for motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants.

articleTitle: Is the Affine Space Determined by Its Automorphism Group?
abstract: In this note we study the problem of characterizing the complex affine space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{A}}^n$</tex> via its automorphism group. We prove the following. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be an irreducible quasi-projective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional variety such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Aut}(X)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Aut}({\mathbb{A}}^n)$</tex> are isomorphic as abstract groups. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is either quasi-affine and toric or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is smooth with Euler characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi (X) \neq 0$</tex> and finite Picard group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Pic}(X)$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{A}}^n$</tex>. The main ingredient is the following result. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be a smooth irreducible quasi-projective variety of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> with finite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Pic}(X)$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> admits a faithful <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\mathbb{Z}} / p {\mathbb{Z}})^n$</tex>-action for a prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi (X)$</tex> is not divisible by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, then the identity component of the centralizer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Cent}_{\operatorname{Aut}(X)}( ({\mathbb{Z}} / p {\mathbb{Z}})^n)$</tex> is a torus.

articleTitle: Asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau metrics with cone singularities along a compact divisor
abstract: We construct Asymptotically Locally Euclidean (ALE) and, more generally, asymptotically conical Calabi–Yau metrics with cone singularities along a compact simple normal crossing divisor. In particular, this includes the case of the minimal resolution of 2D quotient singularities for any finite subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \subset U(2)$</tex> acting freely on the three-sphere, hence generalizing Kronheimer's construction of smooth ALE gravitational instantons.

articleTitle: Bar Category of Modules and Homotopy Adjunction for Tensor Functors
abstract: Given a differentially graded (DG)-category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex>, we introduce the bar category of modules <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{\textbf{{Mod}}}-{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex>. It is a DG enhancement of the derived category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D({{\mathcal{A}}})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex>, which is isomorphic to the category of DG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex>-modules with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A_{\infty }}$</tex>-morphisms between them. However, it is defined intrinsically in the language of DG categories and requires no complex machinery or sign conventions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A_{\infty }}$</tex>-categories. We define for these bar categories Tensor and Hom bifunctors, dualisation functors, and a convolution of twisted complexes. The intended application is to working with DG-bimodules as enhancements of exact functors between triangulated categories. As a demonstration, we develop a homotopy adjunction theory for tensor functors between derived categories of DG categories. It allows us to show in an enhanced setting that given a functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> with left and right adjoints <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>, the functorial complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$FR \xrightarrow{F{\operatorname{act}}{R}} FRFR \xrightarrow{FR{\operatorname{tr}} - {\operatorname{tr}}{FR}} FR \xrightarrow{{\operatorname{tr}}} {\operatorname{Id}}$</tex> lifts to a canonical twisted complex whose convolution is the square of the spherical twist of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. We then write down four induced functorial Postnikov systems computing this convolution.

articleTitle: The Normal Distribution Is Freely Self-decomposable
abstract: The class of self-decomposable distributions in free probability theory was introduced by Barndorff–Nielsen and Thorbj⊘rnsen. It constitutes a fairly large subclass of the freely infinitely divisible distributions, but so far specific examples have been limited to Wigner's semicircle distributions, the free stable distributions, two kinds of free gamma distributions and a few other examples. In this article, we prove that the (classical) normal distributions are freely self-decomposable. More generally it is established that the Askey–Wimp–Kerov distribution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu_c$</tex> is freely self-decomposable for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[-1,0]$</tex>. The main ingredient in the proof is a general characterization of the freely self-decomposable distributions in terms of the derivative of their free cumulant transform.

articleTitle: String Principal Bundles and Courant Algebroids
abstract: Just like Atiyah Lie algebroids encode the infinitesimal symmetries of principal bundles, exact Courant algebroids encode the infinitesimal symmetries of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-gerbes. At the same time, transitive Courant algebroids may be viewed as the higher analog of Atiyah Lie algebroids and the noncommutative analog of exact Courant algebroids. In this article, we explore what the “principal bundles” behind transitive Courant algebroids are, and they turn out to be principal 2-bundles of string groups. First, we construct the stack of principal 2-bundles of string groups with connection data. We prove a lifting theorem for the stack of string principal bundles with connections and show the multiplicity of the lifts once they exist. This is a differential geometrical refinement of what is known for string structures by Redden, Waldorf, and Stolz–Teichner. We also extend the result of Bressler and Chen et al. on extension obstruction involving transitive Courant algebroids to the case of transitive Courant algebroids with connections, as a lifting theorem with the description of multiplicity once liftings exist. At the end, we build a morphism between these two stacks. The morphism turns out to be neither injective nor surjective in general, which shows that the process of associating the “higher Atiyah algebroid” loses some information and at the same time, only some special transitive Courant algebroids come from string bundles.

articleTitle: Open Saito Theory for A and D Singularities
abstract: A well-known construction of B. Dubrovin and K. Saito endows the parameter space of a universal unfolding of a simple singularity with a Frobenius manifold structure. In our paper, we present a generalization of this construction for the singularities of types <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> that gives a solution of the open WDVV equations. For the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>-singularity, the resulting solution describes the intersection numbers on the moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>-spin disks, introduced recently in a work of the 2nd author, E. Clader and R. Tessler. In the 2nd part of the paper, we describe the space of homogeneous polynomial solutions of the open WDVV equations associated to the Frobenius manifolds of finite irreducible Coxeter groups.

articleTitle: Resolutions of Proper Riemannian Lie Groupoids
abstract: In this paper we prove that every proper Lie groupoid admits a regularization to a regular proper Lie groupoid. When equipped with a Riemannian metric, we show that it admits regularization to a regular Riemannian proper Lie groupoid, arbitrarily close to the original one in the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between the quotient spaces. We construct the regularization via a successive blow-up construction on a proper Lie groupoid. We also prove that our construction of the regularization is invariant under Morita equivalence of groupoids, showing that it is a desingularization of the underlying differentiable stack.

articleTitle: The Distribution of H8-Extensions of Quadratic Fields
abstract: We compute all the moments of a normalization of the function that counts unramified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{8}$</tex>-extensions of quadratic fields, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{8}$</tex> is the quaternion group of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8$</tex>, and show that the values of this function determine a point mass distribution. As a consequence toward non-abelian Cohen–Lenstra heuristics of 2-groups, we show this implies that the probability is 0 for any fixed group to appear as the subgroup of the Galois group of the maximal unramified 2-extension fixing the genus field of the quadratic field. Our method additionally can be used to determine the asymptotics of the unnormalized counting function, which we also do for unramified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{8}$</tex>-extensions. Furthermore, we propose that a similar normalization of the counting function is necessary to obtain finite moments when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{8}$</tex> is replaced by any 2-group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>.

articleTitle: On a Class of Kato Manifolds
abstract: We revisit Brunella's proof of the fact that Kato surfaces admit locally conformally Kähler metrics, and we show that it holds for a large class of higher-dimensional complex manifolds containing a global spherical shell. On the other hand, we construct manifolds containing a global spherical shell that admit no locally conformally Kähler metric. We consider a specific class of these manifolds, which can be seen as a higher-dimensional analogue of Inoue–Hirzebruch surfaces, and study several of their analytical properties. In particular, we give new examples, in any complex dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geq 3$</tex>, of compact non-exact locally conformally Kähler manifolds with algebraic dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-2$</tex>, algebraic reduction bimeromorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-2}$</tex>, and admitting nontrivial holomorphic vector fields.

articleTitle: Feigin–Frenkel Image of Witten–Kontsevich Points
abstract: The Witten–Kontsevich KdV tau function of topological gravity has a generalization to an arbitrary Drinfeld–Sokolov hierarchy associated to a simple complex Lie algebra. Using the Feigin–Frenkel isomorphism we describe the affine opers describing such generalized Witten–Kontsevich functions in terms of Segal–Sugawara operators associated to the Langlands dual Lie algebra. In the case where the Lie algebra is simply laced there is a second role these Segal–Sugawara operators play: their action, in the basic representation of the affine algebra associated to the Lie algebra, singles out the Witten–Kontsevich tau function within the phase space. We show that these two Langlands dual roles of Segal–Sugawara operators correspond to a duality between the first and last operator for a complete set of Segal–Sugawara operators.

articleTitle: The Trace Field of Hyperbolic Gluings
abstract: We determine the adjoint trace field of gluings of general hyperbolic manifolds. This provides a new method to prove the nonarithmeticity of gluings, which can be applied to the classical construction of Gromov and Piatetski-Shapiro (and generalizations) as well as certain gluings of pieces of commensurable arithmetic manifolds. As an application, we give many new examples of nonarithmetic gluings and prove that the unique nonarithmetic Coxeter 5-simplex is not commensurable to any gluing of arithmetic pieces.

articleTitle: Complete Ricci Solitons via Estimates on the Soliton Potential
abstract: In this paper, a growth estimate on the soliton potential is shown for a large class of cohomogeneity one manifolds. This is used to construct continuous families of complete steady and expanding Ricci solitons in the setups of Lü–Page–Pope [24] and Dancer–Wang [17]. It also provides a different approach to the two summands system [30] that applies to all known geometric examples.

articleTitle: The Automorphic Discrete Spectrum of Mp4
abstract: We prove the multiplicity formula for the automorphic discrete spectrum of the metaplectic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Mp}_4$</tex> of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Invariants of a General Branched Cover of P1
abstract: We investigate the resolution of a general branched cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \colon C \to \mathbf{P}^1$</tex> in its relative canonical embedding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C \subset \mathbf{P} E$</tex>. We conjecture that the syzygy bundles appearing in the resolution are balanced for a general cover, provided that the genus is sufficiently large compared to the degree. We prove this for the Casnati–Ekedahl bundle, or bundle of quadrics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>—the 1st bundle appearing in the resolution of the ideal of the relative canonical embedding. Furthermore, we prove the conjecture for all syzygy bundles in the resolution when the genus satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g = 1 \mod d$</tex>.

articleTitle: Green Functions for the Pressure of Stokes Systems
abstract: We study Green functions for the pressure of stationary Stokes systems in a (possibly unbounded) domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\ge 2$</tex>. We construct the Green function when coefficients are merely measurable in one direction and have Dini mean oscillation in the other directions and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega $</tex> is such that the divergence equation is solvable there. We also establish global pointwise bounds for the Green function and its derivatives when coefficients have Dini mean oscillation and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega $</tex> has a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{1,\textrm{Dini}}$</tex> boundary. Green functions for the flow velocity of Stokes systems are also considered.

articleTitle: On the Distribution of Periods of Holomorphic Cusp Forms and Zeroes of Period Polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we determine the limiting distribution of the image of the Eichler–Shimura map or equivalently the limiting joint distribution of the coefficients of the period polynomials associated to a fixed cusp form. The limiting distribution is shown to be the distribution of a certain transformation of two independent random variables both of which are equidistributed on the circle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$</tex>, where the transformation is connected to the additive twist of the cuspidal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-function. Furthermore, we determine the asymptotic behavior of the zeroes of the period polynomials of a fixed cusp form. We use the method of moments and the main ingredients in the proofs are additive twists of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions and bounds for both individual and sums of Kloosterman sums.

articleTitle: Berezin–Toeplitz Quantization and the Least Unsharpness Principle
abstract: We show that compatible almost-complex structures on symplectic manifolds correspond to optimal positive quantizations.

articleTitle: On the Positive Theory of Groups Acting on Trees
abstract: In this paper, we study the positive theory of groups acting on trees and show that under the presence of weak small cancellation elements, the positive theory of the group is trivial, that is, coincides with the positive theory of a non-abelian free group. Our results apply to a wide class of groups, including non-virtually solvable fundamental groups of 3-manifold groups, generalised Baumslag–Solitar groups and almost all one-relator groups and graph products of groups. It follows that groups in the class satisfy a number of algebraic properties: for instance, their verbal subgroups have infinite width and, although some groups in the class are simple, they cannot be boundedly simple. In order to prove these results, we describe a uniform way for constructing (weak) small cancellation tuples from (weakly) stable elements. This result of interest in its own is fundamental to obtain corollaries of general nature such as a quantifier reduction for positive sentences or the preservation of the non-trivial positive theory under extensions of groups.

articleTitle: Joint Eigenfunctions for the Relativistic Calogero–Moser Hamiltonians of Hyperbolic Type. III. Factorized Asymptotics
abstract: In the two preceding parts of this series of papers, we introduced and studied a recursion scheme for constructing joint eigenfunctions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_N(a_+, a_-,b;x,y)$</tex> of the Hamiltonians arising in the integrable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-particle systems of hyperbolic relativistic Calogero–Moser type. We focused on the 1st steps of the scheme in Part I and on the cases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=3$</tex> in Part II. In this paper, we determine the dominant asymptotics of a similarity-transformed function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{E}_N(b;x,y)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y_j-y_{j+1}\to \infty $</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j=1,\ldots , N-1$</tex> and thereby confirm the long-standing conjecture that the particles in the hyperbolic relativistic Calogero–Moser system exhibit soliton scattering. This result generalizes a main result in Part II to all particle numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N>3$</tex>.

articleTitle: Bounding Tangencies of Sections on Elliptic Surfaces
abstract: Given an elliptic surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{E}\to \mathcal{C}$</tex> over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of characteristic zero equipped with zero section <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O$</tex> and another section <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> of infinite order, we give a simple and explicit upper bound on the number of points where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O$</tex> is tangent to a multiple of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>.

articleTitle: Hausdorff Dimension in Inhomogeneous Diophantine Approximation
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> be an irrational real number. We show that the set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon $</tex>-badly approximable numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \textrm{Bad}^\varepsilon (\alpha):= \Big\{x\in [0,1]\,: \, \liminf_{|q| \to \infty} |q| \cdot \| q\alpha -x \| \geq \varepsilon \Big\} \end{equation*}$$</tex>has full Hausdorff dimension for some positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon $</tex> if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> is singular on average. The condition is equivalent to the average <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{1}{k} \sum _{i=1, \cdots, k} \log a_i$</tex> of the logarithms of the partial quotients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_i$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> going to infinity with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. We also consider one-sided approximation, obtain a stronger result when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_i$</tex> tends to infinity, and establish a partial result in higher dimensions.

articleTitle: Sharp Green's Function Estimates on Hadamard Manifolds and Adams Inequality
abstract: In this article, we establish estimates on Riesz-type kernels and prove the Adams-type inequality for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{k,p}(M)$</tex> functions, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,g)$</tex> is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature bounded from below and above by a negative constant and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is an integer satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kp=n$</tex>.

articleTitle: Infinite Geodesics of Sub-Finsler Distances in Heisenberg Groups
abstract: We consider Heisenberg groups equipped with a sub-Finsler metric. Using methods of optimal control theory we prove that in this geometric setting the infinite geodesics are horizontal lines under the assumption that the sub-Finsler metric is defined by a strictly convex norm. This answers a question posed in [8] and has applications in the characterization of isometric embeddings into Heisenberg groups.

articleTitle: Rigid Sides of Approximately Finite-Dimensional Simple Operator Algebras in Non-Separable Category
abstract: Applying Popa's orthogonality method to a new class of groups, we construct amenable group factors that are prime and have no infinite-dimensional regular abelian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ast$</tex>-subalgebras. By adjusting Farah–Katsura's solution of Dixmier's problem to the von Neumann algebra setting, we obtain the 1st examples of prime approximately finite-dimensional factors and tensorially prime simple AF-algebras. Our results are proved in Zermelo—Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice (ZFC), thus in particular answering questions asked by Farah–Hathaway–Katsura–Tikuisis. We also directly determine central sequences of certain crossed products. This concludes the failure of the Kirchberg <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}_{\infty }$</tex>-absorption theorem in the non-separable setting.

articleTitle: On Automorphisms of Moduli Spaces of Parabolic Vector Bundles
abstract: Fix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 5$</tex> general points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_1, \dots , p_n\in{\mathbb{P}}^1$</tex> and a weight vector <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{A}} = (a_{1}, \dots , a_{n})$</tex> of real numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \leq a_{i} \leq 1$</tex>. Consider the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}_{{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex> parametrizing rank two parabolic vector bundles with trivial determinant on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\big ({\mathbb{P}}^1, p_1,\dots , p_n\big )$</tex> that are semistable with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{A}}$</tex>. Under some conditions on the weights, we determine and give a modular interpretation for the automorphism group of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}_{{\mathcal{A}}}$</tex>. It is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left (\frac{\mathbb{Z}}{2\mathbb{Z}}\right )^{k}$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\in \{0,\dots , n-1\}$</tex> and is generated by admissible elementary transformations of parabolic vector bundles. The largest of these automorphism groups, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k=n-1$</tex>, occurs for the central weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{A}}_{F}= \left (\frac{1}{2},\dots ,\frac{1}{2}\right )$</tex>. The corresponding moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal M}_{{\mathcal{A}}_F}$</tex> is a Fano variety of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-3$</tex>, which is smooth if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is odd, and has isolated singularities if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is even.

articleTitle: Decompositions of Grothendieck Polynomials
abstract: We investigate the long-standing problem of finding a combinatorial rule for the Schubert structure constants in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory of flag varieties (in type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>). The Grothendieck polynomials of A. Lascoux–M.-P. Schützenberger (1982) serve as polynomial representatives for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theoretic Schubert classes; however no positive rule for their multiplication is known in general. We contribute a new basis for polynomials (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables) which we call glide polynomials, and give a positive combinatorial formula for the expansion of a Grothendieck polynomial in this basis. We then provide a positive combinatorial Littlewood–Richardson rule for expanding a product of Grothendieck polynomials in the glide basis. Our techniques easily extend to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Grothendieck polynomials of S. Fomin–A. Kirillov (1994), representing classes in connective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory, and we state our results in this more general context.

articleTitle: The L2 Weak Sequential Convergence of Radial Focusing Mass Critical NLS Solutions with Mass Above the Ground State
abstract: We study the non-scattering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{2}$</tex> solution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> to the radial focusing mass-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation with mass just above the ground state, and show that there exists a time sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{t_{n}\}_{n}$</tex>, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u(t_{n})$</tex> weakly converges to the ground state <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> up to scaling and phase transformation. We also give some partial results on the mass concentration phenomena of the minimal mass blow-up solution.

articleTitle: The q-Hahn PushTASEP
abstract: We introduce the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Hahn PushTASEP—an integrable stochastic interacting particle system that is a three-parameter generalization of the PushTASEP, a well-known close relative of the TASEP (totally asymmetric simple exclusion process). The transition probabilities in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Hahn PushTASEP are expressed through the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_4\phi _3$</tex> basic hypergeometric function. Under suitable limits, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Hahn PushTASEP degenerates to all known integrable (1+1)-dimensional stochastic systems with a pushing mechanism. One can thus view our new system as a pushing counterpart of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Hahn TASEP introduced by Povolotsky [37]. We establish Markov duality relations and contour integral formulas for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Hahn PushTASEP. In a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\to 1$</tex> limit of our process we arrive at a random recursion, which, in a special case, appears to be similar to the inverse-Beta polymer model. However, unlike in recursions for Beta polymer models, the weights (i.e., the coefficients of the recursion) in our model depend on the previous values of the partition function in a nontrivial manner.

articleTitle: Derived Functors of Differential Operators
abstract: In their work on differential operators in positive characteristic, Smith and Van den Bergh define and study the derived functors of differential operators; these arise naturally as obstructions to differential operators reducing to positive characteristic. In this paper, we provide formulas for the ring of differential operators as well as these derived functors of differential operators. We apply these descriptions to show that differential operators behave well under reduction to positive characteristic under certain hypotheses. We show that these functors also detect a number of interesting properties of singularities.

articleTitle: Basepoint Free Cycles on 0n from Gromov–Witten Theory
abstract: Basepoint free cycles on the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\operatorname{M}}_{0,n}$</tex> of stable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-pointed rational curves, defined using Gromov–Witten invariants of smooth projective homogeneous spaces are introduced and studied. Intersection formulas to find classes are given. Gromov–Witten divisors for projective space are shown equivalent to conformal blocks divisors for type A at level 1.

articleTitle: Approximating Simple Locally Compact Groups by Their Dense Locally Compact Subgroups
abstract: The class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{S}$</tex> of totally disconnected locally compact (tdlc) groups that are non-discrete, compactly generated, and topologically simple contains many compelling examples. In recent years, a general theory for these groups, which studies the interaction between the compact open subgroups and the global structure, has emerged. In this article, we study the non-discrete tdlc groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> that admit a continuous embedding with dense image into some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G\in \mathscr{S}$</tex>; that is, we consider the dense locally compact subgroups of groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G\in \mathscr{S}$</tex>. We identify a class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{R}$</tex> of almost simple groups that properly contains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{S}$</tex> and is moreover stable under passing to a non-discrete dense locally compact subgroup. We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{R}$</tex> enjoys many of the same properties previously obtained for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{S}$</tex> and establish various original results for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{R}$</tex> that are also new for the subclass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{S}$</tex>, notably concerning the structure of the local Sylow subgroups and the full automorphism group.

articleTitle: Segre Indices and Welschinger Weights as Options for Invariant Count of Real Lines
abstract: In our previous paper [5] we have elaborated a certain signed count of real lines on real hypersurfaces of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n-1$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^{n+1}$</tex>. Contrary to the honest “cardinal” count, it is independent of the choice of a hypersurface and, by this reason, provides a strong lower bound on the honest count. In this count the contribution of a line is its local input to the Euler number of a certain auxiliary vector bundle. The aim of this paper is to present other, in a sense more geometric, interpretations of this local input. One of them results from a generalization of Segre species of real lines on cubic surfaces and another from a generalization of Welschinger weights of real lines on quintic three-folds.

articleTitle: Spectral Data for Spin Higgs Bundles
abstract: In this paper we determine the spectral data parametrizing Higgs bundles in a generic fiber of the Hitchin map for the case where the structure group is the special Clifford group with fixed Clifford norm. These are spin and “twisted” spin Higgs bundles. The method used relates variations in spectral data with respect to the Hecke transformations for orthogonal bundles introduced by Abe. The explicit description also recovers a result from the geometric Langlands program, which states that the fibers of the Hitchin map are the dual abelian varieties to the corresponding fibers of the moduli spaces of projective orthogonal Higgs bundles (in the even case) and projective symplectic Higgs bundles (in the odd case).

articleTitle: Multi-directed Graph Complexes and Quasi-isomorphisms Between Them II: Sourced Graphs
abstract: We prove that the projection from graph complex with at least one source to oriented graph complex is a quasi-isomorphism, showing that homology of the “sourced” graph complex is also equal to the homology of standard Kontsevich's graph complex. This result may have applications in theory of multi-vector fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\textrm{poly}}^{\geq 1}$</tex> of degree at least one, and to the hairy graph complex that computes the rational homotopy of the space of long knots. The result is generalized to multi-directed graph complexes, showing that all such graph complexes are quasi-isomorphic. These complexes play a key role in the deformation theory of multi-oriented props recently invented by Sergei Merkulov. We also develop a theory of graph complexes with arbitrary edge types.

articleTitle: A Polynomial Sieve and Sums of Deligne Type
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in \mathbb{Z}[T]$</tex> be any polynomial of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d>1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F\in \mathbb{Z}[X_{0},...,X_{n}]$</tex> an irreducible homogeneous polynomial of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e>1$</tex> such that the projective hypersurface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V(F)$</tex> is smooth. In this paper we present a new bound for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N(f,F,B):=|\{\textbf{x}\in \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}:\max _{0\leq i\leq n}|x_{i}|\leq B,\exists t\in \mathbb{Z}\textrm{ such that}\ f(t)=F(\textbf{x})\}|.$</tex> To do this, we introduce a generalization of the power sieve [14, 28] and we extend two results by Deligne and Katz on estimates for additive and multiplicative characters in many variables.

articleTitle: Boundary Convex Cocompactness and Stability of Subgroups of Finitely Generated Groups
abstract: A Kleinian group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma < \mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb H^3)$</tex> is called convex cocompact if any orbit of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb H^3$</tex> is quasiconvex or, equivalently, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> acts cocompactly on the convex hull of its limit set in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial \mathbb H^3$</tex>. Subgroup stability is a strong quasiconvexity condition in finitely generated groups which is intrinsic to the geometry of the ambient group and generalizes the classical quasiconvexity condition above. Importantly, it coincides with quasiconvexity in hyperbolic groups and convex cocompactness in mapping class groups. Using the Morse boundary, we develop an equivalent characterization of subgroup stability which generalizes the above boundary characterization from Kleinian groups.

articleTitle: Oscillatory Behavior of Large Eigenvalues in Quantum Rabi Models
abstract: We investigate the large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> asymptotics of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-th eigenvalue for a class of unbounded self-adjoint operators defined by infinite Jacobi matrices with discrete spectrum. In the case of the quantum Rabi model we obtain the 1st three terms of the asymptotics that determine the parameters of the model. This paper is based on our previous paper [5] that it completes and improves.

articleTitle: On Integral Cohomology of Certain Orbifolds
abstract: The CW-complex structure of certain spaces, such as effective orbifolds, can be too complicated for computational purposes. In this paper we develop the concept of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{q}$</tex>-CW complex structure on an orbifold, to detect torsion in its integral cohomology. The main result can be applied to well-known classes of orbifolds or algebraic varieties having orbifold singularities, such as toric orbifolds, simplicial toric varieties, torus orbifolds, and weighted Grassmannians.

articleTitle: Arithmetic of Rational Points and Zero-cycles on Products of Kummer Varieties and K3 Surfaces
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be a number field. In the spirit of a result by Yongqi Liang, we relate the arithmetic of rational points over finite extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> to that of zero-cycles over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> for Kummer varieties over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. For example, for any Kummer variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>, we show that if the Brauer–Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to the Hasse principle for rational points on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over all finite extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>, then the (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-primary) Brauer–Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to the Hasse principle for zero-cycles of any given odd degree on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. We also obtain similar results for products of Kummer varieties, K3 surfaces, and rationally connected varieties.

articleTitle: The Non-selfadjoint Approach to the Hao–Ng Isomorphism
abstract: In an earlier work, the authors proposed a non-selfadjoint approach to the Hao–Ng isomorphism problem for the full crossed product, depending on the validity of two conjectures stated in the broader context of crossed products for operator algebras. By work of Harris and Kim, we now know that these conjectures in the generality stated may not always be valid. In this paper we show that in the context of hyperrigid tensor algebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}^*$</tex>-correspondences, each one of these conjectures is equivalent to the Hao–Ng problem. This is accomplished by studying the representation theory of non-selfadjoint crossed products of C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^*$</tex>-correspondence dynamical systems; in particular we show that there is an appropriate dilation theory. A large class of tensor algebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}^*$</tex>-correspondences, including all regular ones, are shown to be hyperrigid. Using Hamana's injective envelope theory, we extend earlier results from the discrete group case to arbitrary locally compact groups; this includes a resolution of the Hao–Ng isomorphism for the reduced crossed product and all hyperrigid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}^*$</tex>-correspondences. A culmination of these results is the resolution of the Hao–Ng isomorphism problem for the full crossed product and all row-finite graph correspondences; this extends a recent result of Bedos, Kaliszewski, Quigg, and Spielberg.

articleTitle: Popular Progression Differences in Vector Spaces
abstract: Green proved an arithmetic analog of Szemerédi's celebrated regularity lemma and used it to verify a conjecture of Bergelson, Host, and Kra, which sharpens Roth's theorem on three-term arithmetic progressions in dense sets. It shows that for every subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_p^n$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> sufficiently large, the density of three-term arithmetic progressions with some nonzero common difference is at least the random bound (the cube of the set density) up to an additive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon $</tex>. For a fixed odd prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, we prove that the required dimension grows as an exponential tower of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>'s of height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Theta (\log (1/\epsilon ))$</tex>. This improves both the lower and upper bound, and is the first example of a result where a tower-type bound coming from applying a regularity lemma is shown to be necessary.

articleTitle: Colorful Simplicial Depth, Minkowski Sums, and Generalized Gale Transforms
abstract: The colorful simplicial depth of a collection of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d+1$</tex> finite sets of points in Euclidean <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-space is the number of choices of a point from each set such that the origin is contained in their convex hull. We use methods from combinatorial topology to prove a tight upper bound on the colorful simplicial depth. This implies a conjecture of Deza et al. [7]. Furthermore, we introduce colorful Gale transforms as a bridge between colorful configurations and Minkowski sums. Our colorful upper bound then yields a tight upper bound on the number of totally mixed facets of certain Minkowski sums of simplices. This resolves a conjecture of Burton [6] in the theory of normal surfaces.

articleTitle: Poisson–Voronoi Tessellation on a Riemannian Manifold
abstract: In this paper, we consider a Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and the Poisson–Voronoi tessellation generated by the union of a fixed point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_0$</tex> and a Poisson point process of intensity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>.
