We obtain a two-term asymptotic expansion, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> goes to infinity, of the mean number of vertices of the Voronoi cell associated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_0$</tex>. The 1st term of the estimate is equal to the mean number of vertices in the Euclidean setting, while the 2nd term involves the scalar curvature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_0$</tex>. This settles with the proper and rigorous frame the former 2D statement from [19] and extends it to higher dimension. The key tool for proving this result is a new change of variables formula of Blaschke–Petkantschin type in the Riemannian setting, which brings out the Ricci curvatures of the manifold.

articleTitle: On the Stabilization of the Betti Numbers of the Moduli Space of Sheaves on ℙ2
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \geq 2$</tex> be an integer, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> be an integer coprime to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>. We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_2 \geq n + \left \lfloor \frac{r-1}{2r}a^2 + \frac{1}{2}(r^2 + 1) \right \rfloor $</tex>, then the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n$</tex>th Betti numbers of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\mathbb{P}^2,H}(r,aH,c_2)$</tex> stabilize where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H = c_1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Reducibility Result for a Class of Linear Wave Equations on ${\mathbb T}^d$
abstract: We prove a reducibility result for a class of quasi-periodically forced linear wave equations on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional torus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb T}^d$</tex> of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\partial_{tt} v - \Delta v + {\varepsilon} {\cal P}(\omega t)[v] = 0,$$</tex> where the perturbation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}(\omega t)$</tex> is a second order operator of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}(\omega t) = - a(\omega t) \Delta - {\cal R}(\omega t)$</tex>, the frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega \in {\mathbb R}^\nu$</tex> is in some Borel set of large Lebesgue measure, the function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a : {\mathbb T}^\nu \to {\mathbb R}$</tex> (independent of the space variable) is sufficiently smooth and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal R}(\omega t)$</tex> is a time-dependent finite rank operator. This is the first reducibility result for linear wave equations with unbounded perturbations on the higher dimensional torus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb T}^d$</tex>. As a corollary, we get that the linearized Kirchhoff equation at a smooth and sufficiently small quasi-periodic function is reducible.

articleTitle: Evolution Equations for Non-Degenerate 2-Forms
abstract: In this paper we introduce several geometric flows that evolve primarily non-degenerate 2-forms, with the motivation to develop a geometric flow to approach the existence of the symplectic forms on a compact manifold that supports a non-degenerate 2-form. In particular, we introduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}^{\ast }\mathrm{d}$</tex>-flow and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}^{\ast }\mathrm{d}$</tex>-Ricci flow for a compatible pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\omega , J)$</tex> of an almost Hermitian structure. We prove the short time existence and uniqueness of these flows with smooth initial data, and give some examples of long time existence and convergence.

articleTitle: On the K-Theoretic Hall Algebra of a Surface
abstract: In this paper, we define the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theoretic Hall algebra for dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> coherent sheaves on a smooth projective surface, prove that the algebra is associative, and construct a homomorphism to a shuffle algebra introduced by Negut [10].

articleTitle: Property RD and Hypercontractivity for Orthogonal Free Quantum Groups
abstract: We prove that the twisted property RD introduced in [2] fails to hold for all non-Kac type, non-amenable orthogonal free quantum groups. In the Kac case we revisit property RD, proving an analogue of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p-L_2$</tex> non-commutative Khintchine inequality for free groups from [29]. As an application, we give new and improved hypercontractivity and ultracontractivity estimates for the generalized heat semigroups on free orthogonal quantum groups, both in the Kac and non-Kac cases.

articleTitle: The Lambda Invariants at CM Points
abstract: In this paper, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (z_1) -\lambda (z_2)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (z_1)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-\lambda (z_1)$</tex> are all Borcherds products on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X(2) \times X(2)$</tex>. We then use the big CM value formula of Bruinier, Kudla, and Yang to give explicit factorization formulas for the norms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (\frac{d+\sqrt d}2)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-\lambda (\frac{d+\sqrt d}2)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (\frac{d_1+\sqrt{d_1}}2) -\lambda (\frac{d_2+\sqrt{d_2}}2)$</tex>, with the latter under the condition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d_1, d_2)=1$</tex>. Finally, we use these results to show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (\frac{d+\sqrt d}2)$</tex> is always an algebraic integer and can be easily used to construct units in the ray class field of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}(\sqrt{d})$</tex> of modulus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>. In the process, we also give explicit formulas for a whole family of local Whittaker functions, which are of independent interest.

articleTitle: Weak Generalized Lifting Property, Bruhat Intervals, and Coxeter Matroids
abstract: We provide a weaker version of the generalized lifting property that holds in complete generality for all Coxeter groups, and we use it to show that every parabolic Bruhat interval of a finite Coxeter group is a Coxeter matroid. We also describe some combinatorial properties of the associated polytopes.

articleTitle: Signatures of Topological Branched Covers
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^4$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y^4$</tex> be smooth manifolds and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: X\to Y$</tex> a branched cover with branching set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>. Classically, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> is smoothly embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, the signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma (X)$</tex> can be computed from data about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and the local degrees of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is an irregular dihedral cover and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\subset Y$</tex> smoothly embedded away from a cone singularity whose link is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>, the second author gave a formula for the contribution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Xi (K)$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma (X)$</tex> resulting from the non-smooth point. We extend the above results to the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is a topological four-manifold and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> is locally flat, away from the possible singularity. Owing to the presence of points on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> which are not locally flat, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> in this setting is a stratified pseudomanifold, and we use the intersection homology signature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma _{IH}(X)$</tex>. For any knot <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> whose determinant is not <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1$</tex>, a homotopy ribbon obstruction is derived from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Xi (K)$</tex>, providing a new technique to potentially detect slice knots that are not ribbon.

articleTitle: McShane-Type Identities for Quasifuchsian Representations of Nonorientable Surfaces
abstract: We show that Norbury's McShane identity for nonorientable cusped hyperbolic surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> generalizes to quasifuchsian representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _1(N)$</tex> as well as pseudo-Anosov mapping Klein bottles with singular fibers given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>.

articleTitle: Local Langlands Correspondence for Regular Supercuspidal Representations of GL(n)
abstract: In this paper, we prove the coincidence of Kaletha's recent construction of the local Langlands correspondence for regular supercuspidal representations with Harris–Taylor's one in the case of general linear groups. The keys are Bushnell–Henniart's essentially tame local Langlands correspondence and Tam's result on Bushnell–Henniart's rectifiers. By combining them, our problem is reduced to an elementary root-theoretic computation on the difference between Kaletha's and Tam's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi $</tex>-data.

articleTitle: A Random Matrix Approach to Absorption in Free Products
abstract: This paper gives a free entropy theoretic perspective on amenable absorption results for free products of tracial von Neumann algebras. In particular, we give the 1st free entropy proof of Popa's famous result that the generator MASA in a free group factor is maximal amenable, and we partially recover Houdayer's results on amenable absorption and Gamma stability. Moreover, we give a unified approach to all these results using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-bounded entropy. We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{M}} = {\mathcal{P}} * {\mathcal{Q}}$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{P}}$</tex> absorbs any subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{M}}$</tex> that intersects it diffusely and that has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-bounded entropy zero (which includes amenable and property Gamma algebras as well as many others). In fact, for a subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{P}} \leq{\mathcal{M}}$</tex> to have this absorption property, it suffices for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{M}}$</tex> to admit random matrix models that have exponential concentration of measure and that “simulate” the conditional expectation onto <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{P}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Reflective Modular Forms: A Jacobi Forms Approach
abstract: We give an explicit formula to express the weight of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-reflective modular forms. We prove that there is no <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-reflective lattice of signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,n)$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 15$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\neq 19$</tex> except the even unimodular lattices of signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,18)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,26)$</tex>. As applications, we give a simple proof of Looijenga's theorem that the lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2U\oplus 2E_8(-1)\oplus \langle -2n\rangle $</tex> is not <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-reflective if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n>1$</tex>. We also classify reflective modular forms on lattices of large rank and the modular forms with the simplest reflective divisors.

articleTitle: Random Waves On $\mathbb T^3$: Nodal Area Variance and Lattice Point Correlations
abstract: We consider the ensemble of random Gaussian Laplace eigenfunctions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{T}^3=\mathbb{R}^3/\mathbb{Z}^3$</tex> (“3 dimensional arithmetic random waves”), and study the distribution of their nodal surface area. The expected area is proportional to the square root of the eigenvalue, or “energy”, of the eigenfunction. We show that the nodal area variance obeys an asymptotic law. The resulting asymptotic formula is closely related to the angular distribution and correlations of lattice points lying on spheres.

articleTitle: The Continuity Method on Minimal Elliptic Kähler Surfaces
abstract: We prove that, on a minimal elliptic Kähler surface of Kodaira dimension one, the continuity method introduced by La Nave and Tian [19] starting from any initial Kähler metric converges in Gromov–Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the generalized Kähler–Einstein metric on its canonical model constructed by Song and Tian [26].
